name: CRHQ
subcategory: AI agent deployment and orchestration platform
tagline: Run a persistent team of AI agents with skills, scheduled jobs, memory and integrations.

pricing.basis: monthly per satellite, unlimited agents and skills
pricing.notes: Includes a dedicated VPS (4 CPU / 8 GB); higher tiers available.

verdictSummary: One scheduled agent is a weekend project with any modern framework. This is not one agent. The value is the platform underneath a fleet: persistent sessions that survive restarts, a scheduler, a growing skills library, an encrypted credential vault, inter-agent messaging, browser and database access, and the operational plumbing that keeps it all alive on a dedicated box. You can build a single cron'd assistant; rebuilding the orchestration, persistence and skills ecosystem is a product, not a one-shot.
coreLoopDIY: Wire one LLM agent with a few tools to a cron job and have it post results to Slack.
diyTimeEstimate: a weekend for one agent, open-ended for the platform
requirements: an agent framework and a lot of glue for persistence, scheduling and secrets
whatYouLose: persistent multi-agent sessions instead of one stateless script
a scheduler, credential vault and skills library you would build from scratch
inter-agent coordination and a shared memory layer
the hosting, uptime and maintenance of the whole thing
128 prebuilt skills you would otherwise reimplement
moatType: orchestration and persistence platform plus a skills ecosystem
whyPeopleStillPay: A single agent demo hides the real work, which is everything around it: keeping many agents alive and coordinated, remembering across runs, holding secrets safely, scheduling reliably, and not having to operate any of it. That platform is the product; the agent is the easy part.
notes: One agent is buildable in a weekend; the fleet platform underneath is not.
prompt: Build a minimal single-agent runner as a starting point, not a replacement for a platform. Stack: Python 3.11, an LLM SDK (Anthropic or OpenAI), APScheduler for cron, and SQLite for memory. Define one agent with a system prompt, two or three tools (web fetch, a shell command allowlist, and send-email), and a loop that runs on a schedule. Persist conversation and tool results to SQLite so the agent has memory across runs. Load the API key from a .env and never log it. Post each run's summary to a Slack webhook. Include a README that is explicit that this is one agent, not multi-agent orchestration, and that persistence, a credential vault, a skills library, and hosting are all left as exercises. Deliberately out of scope: multiple coordinating agents, a web dashboard, a secrets manager, and any hosting.
